CBSE • CLASS 10 • MATHEMATICS

Ch 3 · Pair of Linear Equations in Two Variables — Practice

Attempt first, then open the answer. Everything here is original practice material mapped to the current syllabus.

MCQs

The pair x + y = 5 and 2x + 2y = 10 represents: (a) intersecting lines (b) parallel lines (c) coincident lines (d) none

(c) Coincident lines. All three ratios equal 1/2.

For what value of k does kx + 3y = 7 and 2x + 6y = 14 have infinitely many solutions? (a) 1 (b) −1 (c) 2 (d) 1/2

(a) 1. We need k/2 = 3/6 = 7/14, and 3/6 = 1/2, so k = 1.

If a boat’s downstream speed is 12 km/h and upstream speed is 8 km/h, its still-water speed is: (a) 10 (b) 4 (c) 2 (d) 20 km/h

(a) 10 km/h. Still-water speed = (downstream + upstream)/2.

Written questions

2 marks Without solving, tell whether 2x − 3y = 7 and 4x − 6y = 14 have a unique solution.

a₁/a₂ = 2/4 = 1/2, b₁/b₂ = −3/−6 = 1/2, c₁/c₂ = (−7)/(−14) = 1/2.
All three ratios are equal, so the lines are coincident — infinitely many solutions, not a unique one.

3 marks Solve by elimination: 3x + 4y = 10 and 2x − 3y = 1.

Multiply the first by 3 and the second by 4: 9x + 12y = 30 and 8x − 12y = 4.
Adding: 17x = 34, so x = 2.
Substituting in the first: 6 + 4y = 10, so y = 1.

5 marks A boat goes 30 km upstream and 44 km downstream in 10 hours. In 13 hours it can go 40 km upstream and 55 km downstream. Find the speed of the stream and of the boat in still water.

Let the still-water speed be x km/h and the stream’s speed be y km/h.
Put u = 1/(x − y) and v = 1/(x + y).
30u + 44v = 10 and 40u + 55v = 13.
Solving gives u = 1/8 and v = 1/11, so x − y = 8 and x + y = 11.
Therefore x = 9.5 km/h and y = 1.5 km/h.

4 marks Five years ago, Nuri was thrice as old as Sonu. Ten years later, Nuri will be twice as old as Sonu. How old are they?

Let Nuri be x and Sonu be y now.
x − 5 = 3(y − 5) ⇒ x − 3y = −10.
x + 10 = 2(y + 10) ⇒ x − 2y = 10.
Subtracting: −y = −20, so y = 20 and x = 50.
Nuri is 50 and Sonu is 20.
